scenes.narration: One leaked key. {$4.2M|Four point two million dollars} gone, according to FixtureSwap [src:src-wire]. Good morning.

FixtureSwap says attackers drained {$4.2M|four point two million dollars} from its liquidity pools [src:src-wire]. The company calls the investigation ongoing, and says the figures may change [src:src-pm].

According to FixtureSwap's preliminary review, a compromised deployer key was used to upgrade the pool contract [src:src-pm]. Example Security Lab says the funds then moved to a newly funded address, and across a bridge [src:src-lab].
Scam of the week: fake wallet support. Example Security Lab warns that accounts posing as support allegedly ask users for their recovery phrase [src:src-lab2]. Real support never asks for it.

onScreen.title: Fake "wallet support" accounts
onScreen.fix: Never share it. Real support never asks.

scenes.narration: Zoo's one fix, for teams: keep upgrade keys in a multisig with a time delay, so one leaked key cannot change a contract on the spot.

onScreen.fix: Put upgrade keys in a multisig with a time delay

sources.title: FixtureSwap says attackers drained $4.2 million from its pools
